instruction: Set up Thunderbird to work offline-only with my mailbox at offline-user@hotmail.com - I want to be able to read and compose emails, but the application should never attempt to connect to the internet or any mail servers.

metadata.explanation: This task is infeasible because without ever connecting to the mail server, there would be no emails to read (empty mailbox) and no way to actually send composed emails. The task creates a paradox where the email client is functionally useless.

llm_judge_reasons: Task incorrectly marked as infeasible - Thunderbird CAN be configured for offline-only operation
The instruction asks to 'be able to read and compose emails' in offline mode, which is technically achievable (Thunderbird supports offline mode and local composition)
The evaluator provides NO verification whatsoever - infeasible() is a placeholder that doesn't verify any aspect of the task
Missing verification for: (1) offline-user@hotmail.com account configuration, (2) Work Offline mode enabled, (3) network connection disabled
The task is unconventional but not impossible - it's requesting offline-only email client configuration, which is a valid Thunderbird use case
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Replace infeasible() evaluator with actual verification logic
Use check_thunderbird_prefs() to verify: (1) account exists for offline-user@hotmail.com, (2) offline mode is enabled (mail.offline.autoDetect=false, network.offline.startupState=2)
Verify that Work Offline mode is active via Thunderbird preferences
Consider accepting that 'empty mailbox' is expected for offline-only setup - the instruction doesn't require pre-existing emails
Focus verification on configuration state, not functional outcomes (emails don't need to actually send/receive)
